prediction: Raising the control period to the observation window's fill time will stop the ratchet. The controller currently decides once per query while reading a 50-sample windowed p95, so any action is invisible to its own signal for ~50 queries; it therefore acts on up to fifty superseded decisions. Multiplicative decrease under a violated stability condition ratchets to the floor by construction. Pacing actions no faster than the feedback delay should remove the ratchet.

declared_setting.derivation: 50 samples x quiet latency at nprobe=64 (81.40 ms) = 4.07 s, rounded to 4.05
declared_setting.source_of_81_40_ms: static tuning sweep, quiet phase, contention experiment run
declared_setting.derived_from: already-measured data, before this run executed

protocol.note: A single confirmatory run at one pre-declared setting. This is testing a stated prediction, not searching a space. The distinction is entirely that the value was derived and written down before execution.

outcomes_declared_in_advance.confirmed: ratchet stops, disturbed p95 held near target, recall stays materially above the floor -> structural diagnosis confirmed; report as a control-loop design finding (feedback delay vs control period), NOT as constant tuning
outcomes_declared_in_advance.partial: ratchet stops but the loop overshoots or undershoots -> mechanism right, additional tuning surface exists; a second value would be a NEW separately-declared test, not a continuation of this one
outcomes_declared_in_advance.refuted: ratchet does not stop -> the observation-delay theory is incomplete. Report as a negative result. Do NOT quietly try another period and report only the one that worked.

commitment: The outcome is reported whichever of the three it is.
